ROM FINDINGS (reproduced byte for byte unless marked; each as the reviews and the fix pass corrected it):
1. **`$c84a` is the COMPLETED list — GEM's zombie list — not a timer list.** azombie pushes on it
   (`$fe3fc6..$fe3ff0`), apret searches it by address (`$fe41f0..$fe4202`). The delays wait on `$9c1a` (adelay
   `$fe55a8`, tchange `$fe4e0e`). `aes/aes.h` named it `AES_TIMER_LIST`; it is `AES_ZOMBIE_LIST` now.
2. **`$c84e` (gl_bpend), RE-DERIVED — the first report's "it never returns to 0, a cancelled multi-click wait leaks
   one" is RETRACTED as stated.** Every reference in the GEM text: +1 in abutton for a wait of more than one click
   (`$fe5648`); -1 while above 1 in evremove (`$fe5150`) AND in ctlmgr, the screen manager's own loop, after its
   evnt_multi — once if its button event came (`$fe4a36`), once if its mouse rectangle did (`$fe4a54`), though its
   own wait asked for one click; cleared by sh_main when deskmain returns (`$feb1e2`), the one place it goes back to
   0; read by b_click alone (`$fe4f72`), zero or not. So while the desktop runs it is never 0 once a multi-click
   wait has been queued (the desktop queues one in its first evnt_multi: the snapshot holds 1), and b_click opens
   the click delay on every press — the desktop's normal state, not a leak. A CANCELLED multi-click wait does leave
   its +1 behind (measured: "every event waited for, the timer comes" ends with 2 and none pending), but not for
   good: each wake of the screen manager by a press or by the mouse entering its rectangle takes one off, down to 1.
   BY READING beyond the two pinned evremove cases and that scenario.
3. **evremove takes ANY EVB's parameter for a click count** (`(e_parm >> 16) & $ff`): a button wait's clicks — and a
   MOUSE wait keeps its rectangle's x there. A mouse wait at x 150 woken while a double-click wait is pending counts
   `$c84e` down; at x 257 (low byte 1) it does not. Both pinned. NOT a delay's ticks (the first report's "or a
   delay's ticks from 131,072 up" was a misreading): a delay reaches evremove from tchange alone, which clears the
   parameter first (`$fe4e28 clr.l 16(a5)`).
4. **apret leaves the high word of ANY freed EVB's answer in `$c792`** (`$fe4266..$fe426e`), which ev_rets hands out
   as the buttons' state (`$fe6858`) — called at `$fe6ba8`, BEFORE ev_multi's first apret (`$fe6bce`): the word is
   STALE, the previous apret's, and after a mouse wait it is the rectangle's WIDTH. Pinned on apret's side;
   ev_multi's side is wave 2's.
5. **doq's read has no bound, and aqueue's read test is "any data", not "enough"**: a waiting reader of more than
   the pipe holds, or one process writing 8 bytes to itself and reading 16, takes the index negative, and doq's
   "move what is left" is lbcopy of that count unsigned — 64 KB of the AES's RAM moved down by the bytes read, the
   Line-F handler's RAM copy with it. MEASURED on the ROM (16 held unless said): a read of 32 returns in 196,732
   instructions, 40 in 196,729, 48 in 196,727 (32 held / 48 read: 196,775) — each landing on an instruction of the
   moved handler that still reaches `unlk; rts`; 20 returns in 259,961 over a rewritten vector page (45 odd
   accesses); 17, 18, 24, 33 of 32, 64, 80 of 64, 129 and 144 of 128, and 16 from an empty pipe never return
   (3,000,000 instructions). The first report's "never returns" was false for its own refusal case. REFUSED BY NAME
   (above).
6. **A pipe call for a process id no PD has** — id 2 before anything was started, or `$100` (a WORD compare: its low
   byte is the shell's id and finds nothing): fpdnm answers 0 and aqueue takes the vector page for the PD. Never
   returns (eight shapes, and through the trap door both ways). REFUSED BY NAME (above). Band 3's "a send to a pid
   with no PD spins", at its source.
7. **AN ODD INDEX after a one-byte write**: appl_write of ONE byte leaves the pipe's index odd, and the next write's
   `cmpi.w #20,(a3)` (`$fe5906`) reads the message's type at an odd address (`$ae97`) — a 68000 address error. The
   shores agree by name: the oracle (no address errors) runs on and its ledger names the one access; the host C
   halts by the accessors' name; the target build makes the same one odd access at the same address and equals the
   ROM's image and registers. No C change is right: on a 68000 both builds fault where the ROM faults. doq's merge
   walk makes another (`$fe591a`, a word at `$6907`) when a queued message's third word wraps its offset (`$7ff0`:
   the step is 16 + that word, AS A WORD).
8. **aqueue serves the first waiter at the other end UNCHECKED — a waiting WRITER overruns the pipe.** 32 bytes
   served after a read of 16 land past the pipe, on the next PD's first 16 bytes, the index reading 144 of 128;
   taken further (232 bytes) the ROM itself rewrites PD1's queue pointer and the spare PD's status and RETURNS. So
   "every PD's queue pointer names its own pipe" and "a spare PD's status is 0" are NOT invariants of the machine —
   pinned ROM-faithfully (C == ROM over the overrun), which is what tells the three spellings of "the pipe" and
   pstart's `clr.w p_stat` apart. And its `ori.w #1` (NOCANCEL) on the served EVB is NOT dead (the first report
   said it was): the served doq runs before azombie's `move.w #2`, and a waiting writer whose buffer is its own EVB
   writes the flag word, NOCANCEL set, into the pipe. A negative index is reachable and returned from too (a write
   of a negative count from a buffer below the pipe); aqueue's room and data tests are signed words.
9. **WAIT LISTS ARE LIFO**: evinsert queues at the HEAD and aqueue serves the head — seen on the mouse wait (a
   second rectangle's EVB found first) and, ON A STAGED APPLICATION ONLY, on a pipe (two writers parked, the last
   queued served first; the scoping saw the same on the lock, waiters [PD2, PD1] → owner PD2, over the same kind of
   stub). Where it concerns a third process it is a staged-application finding, not a claim about a real one.
10. **ap_find's frame is 10 bytes and lstcpy has no bound; the ROM's real boundary is TWELVE characters**, not eleven.
    The 11th lands on the top byte of aes_dispatch's saved A6 (off the 24-bit bus) and its NUL on bits 16..23 —
    already 0, because the trap handler runs the AES on the calling PD's UDA stack (`$fe3eee`) and the three static
    UDAs lie below 64 KB (measured: A6 = `$a1cc` at ap_find's entry; ten against eleven characters differ in ONE
    dead byte, `$a1a4`). `appl_find("CONTROL.ACC")` answers -1 on the ROM and on both builds; twelve never returns
    on the ROM and halts by name on both. THE BAND-5 CAVEAT: an accessory's UDA is the loader's; above 64 KB eleven
    characters zero a live byte of the caller's A6.
11. **getpd with no PD left** — the three static PDs handed out, no accessory loaded — **takes ADDRESS 0 for a PD**:
    id 3 stored at `$1c`, `$c682` counted to 1, uda_insuper's store aimed at ROM. (Shown on a staged application's
    machine; the kit refuses the ROM's own run, "store into the ROM window".)
12. **The spare PD is shadowed by PD0**: it is blank-named with id 0 until pstart numbers it, and PD0's name is eight
    blanks — so fpdnm by id 0 or by eight blanks finds PD0 first, and appl_find of eight blanks answers 0.
13. Smaller, each pinned unless said: azombie stores the WHOLE flag word (2), so a delay's 4, the mouse-leave 8 and
    NOCANCEL are gone once an EVB is completed; signal's two guards are dead on every reachable machine; iasync never
    tests get_evb's 0 (BY READING: it would store through address 0); a wait list's first EVB points back at the
    head "as an EVB" (head less the RAM long `$97f6` = 4); apret matches its mask by EQUALITY, acancel by AND;
    apret's unlink from its process's list stores 0 in every one of the ROM's own calls (ev_multi's aprets take the
    deepest EVB first — the non-zero store is a labelled case); tak_flag's refusal leaves the owner's HIGH word in
    D0 over a cleared low word, takes a free semaphore whatever owner the last release left, and never touches the
    wait list; pd_match compares against an 8-byte COPY ended in its own frame (a name matches only blank-padded to
    eight); doq writes through the PD's queue pointer and reads the message back at `pd + 56`, reads its count ONCE,
    and leaves a merged redraw's bytes in the pipe beyond the index; psetup parks its CALLER's SR in `$8998`; aqueue
    picks its list by `writing XOR ready` on WHOLE words (`$100` picks the writers').

**aes — band 4 wave 1 (phase A): what no C runs yet, what stays unpinned, the labelled cases, three harness rulings,
what is deferred, and the ROM's findings — its KNOWN RACES first.**

NOT RECONSTRUCTED BY THIS WAVE, by design:
- **Nothing after a switch.** The dispatch hook refuses (ruling Q1), so no C runs past dsptch: mwait's return and its
  re-read of rlr, ev_block's apret after a block, unsync's continuation after its yield. What is unheld there is
  DATA, not instructions — each tail is straight-line code shared with the returning road, which is held: a NON-ZERO
  answer of ev_button / ev_mouse / ev_block (non-zero only after a block-then-wake); `$c792` after a woken button
  wait reaching ev_rets through the twin; that the event bit survives the switch in the twin's frame (on target it
  is in A2, which savestate keeps — read off the blob, not tested). Wave 3.
- **ev_timer has no Tier 3 row, by nature** (a delay never returns in one run), **forker none until wave 2** (its
  queue's codes are the ROM's: its row), **drawrat and dsptch none** (hand 68000; dsptch's bytes are pinned, drawrat's
  five instructions ship with wave 2's glue). The target-only `aes_<fn>_fork` entries are run by NO row and swept by
  no host mutant until forker's row exists.

UNPINNED, each with its reason:
- **The input's six survivors, by name**: bchange's CONTROL arm reading gl_cowner and its DESKTOP arm reading window
  0's owner (`bg-control-is-desk`, `bg-desk-is-cowner`, `h-desktop-owner`: both are the desk in every machine — a
  third process owning the screen, band 5); the width of bchange's owner compare (`bg-owner-compare-24`, `-16`: no
  machine holds a tagged or a high PD in gl_mowner); forker's recorder ending on a NON-key entry whose data's high
  word is `$2b1c` (`rec-end-any-fork`: a second process recording, band 5).
- **The interleaved-interrupt sweep lays its interrupt whatever the IPL** (a bench run is entered at IPL 7): a
  routine that MASKS — tchange's and adelay's spl7 bracket — is not swept by it; their brackets are held by Tier 3's
  symmetric SR rule and read off both objects. It takes no boundary INSIDE a callee (each callee is its own case),
  and chkkbd, kchange, bchange and tchange are not cases of it (an audit run on the fixed blob found no state the
  ROM's routine does not leave in kchange and tchange; chkkbd and bchange were out of that run's reach).
- **b_click's two counts are held by a tick taken INSIDE b_click**, which no ST can do (both are the MFP's, level
  6): the case pins the idiom, not a machine. forkq's `addq.w #1,$c906` and b_click's `addq.w #1,$c72c` were
  memory-direct by GCC's own choice before the idiom: no mutant of the target text tells the two spellings apart on
  this compiler.
- **The waits' survivors, by class** (24 of 202): EQUIVALENT — iasync's `pred = 0` and `flag = 0` stores (get_evb has
  just cleared the EVB), adelay's `<=` as `<` and its list head as the literal 4, unsync's owner stored after azombie
  and its wait read before the decrement, and constants of the machine (the tick's 20 ms, pids 0..2); UNREACHABLE
  SHORT OF A POKE — akbin's key count as a byte (nq bounds the queue at 8), an EVB at a `$xx0000` address (unsync's
  wait-list head tested as a long), `clr.l $948e` as a long (65,536 ticks counted with no delay pending); BY RULING —
  unsync's D0 on its still-held and hand-over roads (not the ROM's; nothing reads it); THE ROM'S RUN DOES NOT RETURN
  — a negative length and a negative process id through ap_rdwr (the C refuses by name); AFTER A SWITCH — ev_button
  answering 0; THE HOST STORES NO SR — adelay's bracket removed survives the host batteries and is pinned at Tier 3.
- **The input's equivalents and orders**: a sign-extended sense, the state as a word, post_button's return signed,
  set_mown's post argument on the bus, tchange's next by link, an addend cut to a byte (every caller hands 1 or 3);
  gl_kowner stored before the posts and b_delay called after xrat / yrat are stored (no callee reads either).
- **iasync with no EVB free** (get_evb's 0, which the ROM does not test): 15 EVBs, three processes hold at most ten.
  (Band 4 wave 2: REFUSED BY NAME off target and counted unreachable on any machine the ROM makes — its paragraph.)
- **ev_timer's and ev_dclick's divide with the tick's milliseconds 0**; **a double-click rate whose table index
  leaves the ROM** (the host refuses the read).
- **nq's re-reads of rear and count after the key's store**: equivalent unless the queue aliases itself.
- **`EVDOOR_A_CALL_NOT_A_JUMP` rests on a compiler behaviour**, not a documented barrier: GCC keeps an unused
  `__builtin_return_address(0)` until its tail-call pass. It is held on both blobs and by a probe under both flag

  weight and moved a committed object.
- **Coverage after the fix pass** was not re-measured (the wave log quotes the authors' builds).

THE LABELLED CASES — where a case does NOT stand on a machine the ROM's scheduler made alone:

- ARGUMENT-CLASS MACHINES BY THE ROM'S OWN iasync / apret called more than once for the running process

THREE HARNESS FACTS THIS WAVE RULED ON:
- **THE BOOT SNAPSHOT IS NOT BIT-REPRODUCIBLE ACROSS CAPTURES** (real-time emulation: 451 of 1,048,576 bytes
  differed between the capture of 2026-10-03 and one made 2026-10-06 — hz200, dead stack). Rows are reproducible
  objects PER SNAPSHOT; nothing compares two captures, and any check that hashes rows across trees must pin ONE
  `build/boot_ram.bin` (a review that did not read 48 phantom "moved" rows).
- **THE ZYGOTE'S IMAGE IS GUARDED ON EVERY RUN** — `make test` too, stricter than a worker's own fork: a core that
  indexes out of its image fails its guard BY NAME where before it read the worker's heap. It is what makes a fork
  of another address space a safe stand-in (the unguarded stress was red); the alternative loses the lever in `make
  test`.
- **A TEST THAT TAKES `monkeypatch` RUNS WITH THE DERIVATION CACHE OFF** (autouse): the one rule found that makes "a
  patched derivation is never served" true by construction. A test that patches WITHOUT the fixture and counts ROM
  runs must switch the cache off itself (`derived.DERIVED_OFF`).

DEFERRED, each measured or named:
- **THE 200 s LINE IS HELD WARM AND THROUGH THE MAKEFILE, NOT BY A BARE COLD `pytest`**: 166.7 s warm, 183.6 s as a
  cold `make test` runs it (derivations made first), 212.6 s for a cold `pytest` with nothing made. Of band 3 wave
  3's three parked levers: the content-keyed disk cache is TAKEN; reusing the real-disk run's deliveries for the
  replay is REFUTED as content-neutral (wave log) and replaced by keeping the replay's own; the lighter second
  differential is NOT taken (it drops (EV)'s window vets). Lever E — one differential per distinct content — is
  REFUSED: it would remove the repeated executions that expose order dependence.
- **THE KIT'S HANDLING OF THE 16 MB IMAGE** is what the remaining seconds are (78 % of a battery's serial time; a
  third of the suite's CPU in `sys`): a kit change that copies and compares RAM and the windows a run can write, not
  the 15 MB between RAM and the ROM. ITS OWN FUTURE KIT COMMIT, with the kit's suite and the six other projects'.
- **DOOR CHILDREN ARE STILL FRESH INTERPRETERS** (1,994 a run, 170 CPU-s): the zygote serves a core that reaches no
  hook; it could fork a door child with its hooks bound there. The mechanism is in place, the binding is not.
- **EVERY HOST SLOT A ROUTINE HOLDS ACROSS A WAIT NEEDS ap_rdwr's PER-PROCESS SHAPE AT WAVE 3** (fm_do's, mn_do's,
  fs_input's, the gr_ drag loops' frames while parked in ev_multi): today the fork dies at the hook and nothing sees
  two processes inside one routine. `host_slot_claim_for` is the mechanism; the audit is wave 3's.
- **FLIP 3's known debts** (**Next**): `sr_drops` on door rows that reach a mask bracket through a rebound twin; the
  three bindings the input's battery makes locally, and `$fcff0a`.
- **THE SHADOW IS RETIRED (band 4 wave 3, step R: its entry has the census — 5,473 nested runs a suite run — and the
  mutation table). What stood here until then:** `SHADOWED` is every rebound entry, always — all eight since FLIP 3
  (its shadows a suite run were NOT re-counted:
  the derivation cache serves kept nested runs since wave 2, and flip 2's counter does not survive the zygote's
  forks). At FLIP 2, seven: 3,541 shadows a suite run (1,063 before it), of
  4,873 nested ROM runs (4,927 before: a served call became a shadow, one nested run either way). The suite cost of
  the flip, one quiet sample each side: +1.6 / +3.7 / +3.8 s of pytest's wall (cold bare / in a cold `make test` /
  warm) and +16 / +27 / +38 CPU-s — above the rehearsal's estimate (+5.4 CPU-s: 2.5 ms an arrival), by an amount
  one sample a side cannot tell from the run-to-run spread, which was not measured. If a later flip makes it cost,
  the retire rule must be a rule, not a list.
- **Not memory-direct and left, no race**: evasync.c's `$c84e` decrement (wave 0; b_click only READS the word) and
  the recorder's records-left count (appl_trecord's, process level).
- **The kit's `osh_run_bench` begins with the PREVIOUS run's D0–A6 when no seed is installed** (its comment says so;
  `rom_bench` always seeds): seen while fixing the USP, not changed — no project runs it unseeded.
- **Row order still differs between import orders** (`aes.ROWS` fills in import order; every consumer keys by name);
  the duplicates inside test files (`before(arrival)`, four `_register_rows`, two `RETURN_KEY_CODE`) are not hoisted.
- **`make gates` is not three gates for the wall of one** on ten cores (wave log): one command, one build.

KNOWN ROM RACES — MATCHED, NOT FIXED. Real defects of TOS 1.02 on the machine, each measured on the ROM's own code by
the instruction-boundary sweep; the C leaves the same SET of states at the same windows (equal state sets on both
blobs), neither narrower nor wider:
- **forkq is not interrupt-safe.** Called at process level (chkkbd's key, b_delay under mchange, appl_tplay) with a
  mouse or tick interrupt's forkq landing between `$fe4b2c move.w $c6b0,d0` and `$fe4b44 addq.w #1,$c6b0` — 6 of its
  18 instruction boundaries — both entries are stored in the SAME slot (the interrupt's is overwritten), the tail
  moves two on and the count two up, so forker next calls whatever the skipped slot holds: a stale event of 32
  events ago, or — until the ring has gone round once after boot — code 0: `jsr 0`. The count itself is never lost
  (`addq.w` on memory).
- **The click count's window.** A tick between mchange's push of the click count (`$fe53be`) and b_delay's `sub.w`
  (`$fe4fc0`) — the Line-F call lies in it — leaves the count at `$ffff`: the press is not queued until the count has
  run down again (65,535 ticks) or the next move past the slop ends it. A PRESS in the same window (b_click's
  `addq.w #3`) is counted as a second click and the count goes on for 3 ticks (the ROM's `sub.w` is on memory, so the
  +3 is never lost).
- **b_delay reads the buttons twice** for its second entry (compare `$fe4fea`, push `$fe4ff6`): a press between the
  two queues `bchange(1, 1)` where the compare saw a release.

ROM FINDINGS (reproduced byte for byte; each as the reviews and the fix pass corrected it):
1. **gl_bpend (`$c84e`) is left at 2 after a CANCELLED multi-click wait** (wave 0's finding 2, CONFIRMED with its
   consequence pinned): after "every event waited for, the timer comes" the word is 2 with no button wait pending,
   and b_click — which reads it only as zero / non-zero (`$fe4f72`) — still opens a click count on a press: the press
   is delayed by the whole double-click time (11 ticks in the snapshot) for a process that asked for no double click.
   "A press with nothing pending is queued at once" is reached by no machine of this snapshot.
2. **forkq DROPS the 33rd and the 34th entry** (wave 0's scoping, CONFIRMED on the routine: 34 mouse packets through
   the VDI's ISR and the motion glue, nothing run): the calls store NOTHING and the caller is not told. The same
   queue carries button changes and the timer, so a full queue loses those too. forker counts an entry OUT before it
   calls it, so a fork function can queue one entry into a full queue's just-vacated slot.
3. **`$c792` is the rectangle's WIDTH after a parked mouse wait** (wave 0's finding 4, CONFIRMED and sharper): apret
   leaves the high word of the answer it took; a mouse wait that parked keeps (w, h) in its answer. ev_mouse KNOWS —
   it stores `$c90a` over rets[2] right after ev_rets (`$fe6902`). evnt_multi calls ev_rets BEFORE its aprets, so the
   buttons it answers when no button event came are the word the PREVIOUS wait left: after a mouse wait for a
   20-wide rectangle, the next evnt_multi answers buttons = 20 (pinned on ev_rets's side; ev_multi's is wave 2's).
4. **ap_rdwr answers ev_block's word** — the author's "always answers 0" was WRONG as stated. It is 0 on every path
   a PIPE wait takes (aqueue never stores an EVB answer), which is every call appl_read / appl_write make; handed
   another wait's code — ap_rdwr(5, …) with a key queued — it answers that wait: the key.
5. **unsync's hand-over leaves a STALE PREDECESSOR**: with two waiters it moves the list's head to the second EVB
   and does not rewrite that EVB's predecessor, which still names the EVB just taken off (now on the completed
   list). Harmless while unsync is the list's only taker. It follows the semaphore's list by LINK, not the process's
   NEXT, and sets D0 on ONE road only (nobody waiting: 0).
6. **A NEGATIVE evnt_timer** queues a delay of negative ticks and arms a negative countdown; before a pending delay
   it leaves that one its ticks PLUS the size. evnt_timer(−2^31) waits ONE tick (ldiv's edge); 0..39 ms wait one.
   adelay tests its ticks and the countdown as LONGS (65,536 ticks is a delay) and clears the ticks counted so far
   only when no countdown was running.
7. **ev_dclick's rate is an UNBOUNDED SIGNED INDEX** into the ROM's five-word table: rates −1, −2, 5.. read the
   opcode table's tail, `$ffff` words, the alert table, and make the click delay from them.
8. **iasync with a code outside 1..7** (an unsigned test) leaves an EVB on its process's list and on NO wait list:
   ev_block of such a code blocks for good. A process's NINTH concurrent wait gets event bit `$100`, carried as a
   word everywhere (no ROM caller queues nine: evnt_multi queues six).
9. **A MOBLK's LEAVE flag that is neither 0 nor 1 is always "satisfied"**: amouse completes the wait at once and
   ev_mchk answers 1 — the flag is compared as a word with inside's 0 / 1. (It never reaches a wait list: a queued
   wait carries only bit 3.) amouse reads its rectangle from its COPY and stores into the EVB between two reads of
   it: a MOBLK lying over the EVB the wait takes is overwritten by the first store and the answer still keeps the
   copied w, h.
10. **mchange posts where the VDI says the mouse IS, not where the event says**: it asks vq_mouse and stores and
    posts that point; with two moves queued the FIRST mchange already completes a wait the second's point satisfies,
    and the second posts the same point again. WHILE A RECORDING PLAYS it stores the EVENT's words unclamped:
    appl_tplay of a mouse record at x = −1 leaves the AES's xrat at `$ffff` after it returns.
11. **`$96d8` — the LEAVE word of the screen manager's own MOBLK — is a constant 0**: cleared once by ctlmgr
    (`$fe49ea`), written by nothing else in the GEM text, compared by mchange (`$fe5456`). The hand-over test is in
    effect "inside the ACTIVE menu rectangle" (`$96da`: the titles, not the whole bar).
12. **`$c6ae`, forker's busy byte, is read by NOTHING**: set and cleared by forker, cleared by gem_main (`$fda108`).
13. **`$947a` during appl_tplay is the VDI's `$fcff0a` default_user_cur** (ap_tplay `$fe66ac` saves the VDI's cursor
    vector there), not the snapshot's bare `rts`: drawrat's call queues the point for the VBL when the cursor is
    shown and stores nothing when it is hidden.
14. **The mouse's ownership**: once the mouse is the screen manager's it stays so OFF the bar (mchange only ever
    hands it TO ctl_pd; a press in the control rectangle then goes to the screen manager's button wait); the control
    rectangle is tested BEFORE the menu bar (with the screen owned a press on the bar is the owner's); set_mown
    always posts ONE click, whatever the wait asked for (a desk parked for a double click and handed the mouse back
    with the button down gets a 1-click event); ct_chgown's D0 is always 0.
15. Smaller, each pinned unless said: a wait list is LIFO for evnt_multi's two rectangles too, on a REAL machine (the
    second MOBLK's wait is the list's first); b_delay queues only at EXACTLY 0 (a count stepped past it wraps and
    goes on); downorup's sense is the whole high byte compared with a 0 / 1 (any other sense is always satisfied);
    chkkbd asks the keyboard OWNER's queue and stops polling at 8 (keys beyond stay in the BIOS's buffer; nq's own
    "full" arm is reached by no caller); abutton counts a multi-click wait by the clicks' low byte as an UNSIGNED
    word (128 count); ev_button loses its mask's high byte and ORs its state in whole; mwait answers every event
    that came, not only its mask's; b_click has NO Line-F call word (its one caller is the button glue's `jsr`); the
    snapshot's control rectangle is `(0, 11, 320, 189)`, so every press on the bare desktop is "in control".

**aes — band 4 wave 2 (phase A): one DIVERGENCE refused off target, what is unpriced and why, the glue sites band 5
owes, what stays unpinned BY NAME, what is dead or labelled, two thin margins, what is deferred, and the ROM's
findings.**

A DOCUMENTED DIVERGENCE (ruling U3):
- **PAST THE LAST EVB THE ROM BUILDS THE WAIT AT ADDRESS 0 — refused by name off target** (get_evb's "none", which
  iasync does not test). ARGUMENT-CLASS ONLY: unreachable by counting on any machine the ROM makes — fifteen EVBs and
  five more with each accessory (`$fe4536`), where one blocked call asks six at most (ev_multi) and the screen
  manager's own asks three: 6 + 3 + 6n ≤ 15 + 5n for every n ≤ 6. (The author's "two accessories waiting on every
  event are enough" was WRONG.) **THE COUNT ABOVE IS ITSELF CORRECTED (band 5 wave 0, measured on the ROM's own
  boot):** the FIRST accessory runs in the spare static PD and brings NO EVBs, so the supply is 15 + 5(n − 1), and
  6 + 3 + 6n > 15 + 5(n − 1) from n = 2 on — 21 against 20. So it is NOT unreachable by counting; it needs PD0
  asking 6 (an application, where the desk asks 3) beside two six-way accessories: not booted. The refusal by name
  on the host and the target's plain stores stand as they are. Reached on a staged machine: eight waits of no kind queued by the ROM's own iasync
  leave four EVBs, and evnt_multi asks six. THE ORACLE lets the stores through and parks with the exception vectors'
  page rewritten; a 68000 takes a BUS ERROR at the first (address 0 is ROM): the oracle's answer is not the machine's
  — the low-memory twin of the store above RAM. So the HOST build refuses by name at iasync (`src/aes/evwait.c`,
  "iasync: no EVB is free"), after the four waits the ROM queues before it, with nothing stored at 0
  (`test_past_the_last_evb_the_host_refuses_by_name`: the EVB table equals the ROM's run's, and the oracle's run is
  held to have stored at 0). The TARGET build keeps the ROM's plain stores and takes the bus error the ROM takes
  (`evwait_c.o` byte-identical: the refusal is compiled off target alone).

UNPRICED, and why:
- **The three interrupt glues** (`$fed3be`, `$fed3e4`, `$fed426`): a REGISTER contract, which `RomBench` does not
  hand, and by-nature differences in compared RAM — the private stack's frames — which the transcription relation does
  not drop. Verified by their own differential on both blobs (`vet_the_glue`). **A RULING IS PENDING**: leave them
  unpriced, or build a Tier 3 relation for a register-contract `.S` with named memory drops.
- **gotopgm** (`$fe38b0`): no machine band 4's scheduler makes has a program to enter — the accessory loader's (band
  5). **disp** (`$fe4d9e`) has no row of its own: the table prices no line at its address; the yield's row is
  dsptch's, and its STATUS row is ⚠️ for that reason alone (a ✅ row there reds `test_status`).
- **A row that BLOCKS AND IS WOKEN** is measured on both blobs (`ev_block` for a key typed ahead: 31,690 cycles in the
  ROM, 26,556 ours — ×0.84; shipped ×0.83) and NOT in the table: Tier 3's door stops refuse a run that reaches dsptch
  from a door entry. Rows that switch WITH A DELIVERY or through a foreign process are Tier 1 only (the host's model).
  Wave 3.

OWED BY ROUTINES NOT RECONSTRUCTED YET (band 5) — every ROM site that names an entry of the switch's kind by value and
is not ours yet (`test_aes_irq.OWED_BY_ROUTINES_NOT_RECONSTRUCTED`, held to the census of the ROM's own code
immediates: a site ported and not re-pointed reds):

  | ROM site | what it names | whose |
  |---|---|---|
  | `$fd9f86` `lea $fed424` → `$947a` | justretf into AES_DRWADDR | gem_main |
  | `$fd9f92` `lea $fed426` → `$947e` | the tick glue, later handed to vex_timv | gem_main |
  | `$fe437c`, `$fed5a6` (gotopgm's address pushed) | gotopgm | the accessory loader, the shell's launch |
  | `$fe6698`, `$fe66b6` `move.l #$fed424` | justretf handed to the VDI | appl_tplay |

and the sites that reach an entry through the Line-F TABLE or a `jsr`, which no census of immediates sees: drawrat
(`$fef1f8`; mchange's call word `$fe5400` — our mchange calls the C), cli / sti (`$fef190` / `$fef198`: gem_main),
spl7_save / spl_restore (`$fef040` / `$fef044` and six `jsr`s: the event layer's C spells them inline). Until those
routines are C the entries `aes_rom_justretf`, `aes_rom_tick_glue`, `aes_rom_gotopgm`, `aes_rom_drawrat`,
`aes_rom_cli`, `aes_rom_sti`, `aes_rom_spl7_save`, `aes_rom_spl_restore` are reached by nothing in our build (pinned
and, where a row can run them, priced). INSTALLED by ours today: `$fe8844` / `$fe884a` (gsx_setmb_aes's two `pea`s:
the motion and the button glue). A recording made under the ROM holds ROM fork-function addresses: played back under
our build, forkq queues them and our forker would `jsr` them — by nature (a recording never survived a TOS version
either). (CORRECTED by band 4 wave 3's step T, which read the two bodies: a FINISHED recording holds NUMBERS — ap_trecd
turns each fork function's address into 0..3 before it returns, and ap_tplay turns the number back into the playing
build's own fork function — so a recording does survive a build. What is queued as it is, and called, is a number
that is NONE OF THE FOUR: a code address of the application's own making. AND THE TABLE'S LAST ROW IS PORTED: our
ap_tplay hands the VDI `aes_rom_justretf` on target (`aes/aptape.h`, `draws_nothing`), held by its rows on both
blobs. The census still carries its two sites, `$fe6698` and `$fe66b6`, as owed by nobody
(`test_aes_rom_data.CODE_IMMEDIATES`, `owed_by` unset; `test_aes_irq.SITES_OWED` counts six): OWED, a re-pointing of
those two rows to `aes/aptape.h` — found by the docs pass, no test reds on it.)

UNPINNED, by name, each with its reason:
- **The message's apret BEFORE the rectangles'** (the review's mutant `j09`): a message AND a rectangle in ONE wake.
  While the writer — the screen manager — is on the bar the mouse is ITS, and the desk's rectangle waits are not
  posted in that wake (three shapes tried: all `$10`). Needs a writer that does not own the mouse (an accessory, band
  5) or wave 3's scheduler taking two wakes in one idle.
- **THE TARGET BUILD'S FRAME ACROSS A REAL SWITCH**: a woken case's "switch" is the host hook's return; on target
  GCC's frame (the waits' bits, the flags, what arrived) is saved and restored by savestate / switchto on the
  process's own stack. The woken cases hold the HOST build's tail, composed with the same call's case AT DSPTCH — not
  the switch itself. Wave 3.
- **Two C processes' QPB slots live at once** (wave 3's audit): held today as "a process id apart" on two separate
  runs. **A host-slot mutant under the zygote** aborts the WORKER, never a test, at the next in-process claim; the
  give-back is held by `test_the_qpb_s_host_slot_is_given_back_when_the_call_returns` (two calls in one fork),
  whatever its order.
- **`aes_switch.IDLE_HOOKS`' forks are the WORKER's** (104 a run, ≈ 1.4 CPU-s), not the zygote's, and cannot be under
  the named-hook contract: a named hook must live in a module the zygote already holds, and it holds no battery's
  helper.
- **The equivalent survivors, argued**: `cancel-answer-dropped` in `evmulti.c` (acancel answers the bits of COMPLETE
  or NOCANCEL waits; a COMPLETE wait's bit is in mwait's answer already, and NOCANCEL is set and completed inside one
  aqueue call) and the review's eighteen (a02 b08 c03 d06 d08 f04 f05 f06 f07 f08 g01 g02 h04 h06 i04 j12 j14 j22 —
  among them a true equivalence worth knowing: with the pipe FULL a pipe index read as a byte takes the WAIT path and
  leaves the fast path's image byte for byte); `id-poll-after` and `yd-lv-guard-decremented` in `evdisp.c`;
  `p-stack-glue-stack-not-restarted` in the stack reading (each `lea <stack top>,sp` is its glue's second instruction,
  nothing pushed before).
- **Two survivors that are NOT this wave's, met by its sweeps and left**: unsync's `answer_compared` arm (wave 1's
  `unsync_answers`: the three rows pass Tier 3 with D0 compared — both shores leave the same D0 on these machines) and
  the handed routines in `aes_evinput.CURSOR_HOOKS` (its one case, drawrat over a staged cursor routine, calls nothing
  else).
- **The parked-QPB vet's equal-address arm does not vet the eight bytes**: tried, it reds three committed
  `test_aes_evwait` cases — a staged machine carries no stack band (the ROM's bytes against our zeros). Reverted,
  pinned with the reason. A wait the MACHINE came with holds one address on both shores and is compared.
- **ONE declared exception to the general guard** (`tier3.ENTERED_BY_THE_MACHINE_S_POINTER`): drawrat's bare-`rts`
  `.S` row runs the ROM's justretf, 16 cycles, because the snapshot's `$947a` holds the ROM's address; the day
  gem_main / appl_tplay install OUR `aes_rom_justretf` on target the declaration goes. (ap_tplay hands the VDI ours
  since band 4 wave 3's step T — for the length of a playback; the snapshot's `$947a` is gem_main's store, band 5's,
  so the declaration stands.) Sliced rows are not asked by
  the guard (a slice is cut from a whole run the ARRIVALS rule already holds call by call).
- **The recorder's buffer at a slice's mark** is not compared modulo the relocation (no session records): a session
  that records would red by name at the mark, not pass. **The SR settling of a DOOR row is unexercised**: no door
  row's ROM run stores an SR save word, before or after flip 3 (measured) — the code that would settle one is named by
  no test.
- **"Milliseconds into ticks" stands twice** (`evlib.c`, `evmulti.c`: `aes_ldiv(image, ms, the tick's ms)` at
  `$fe6942` and `$fe6b6c`) BY A PIN: `test_the_twin_names_the_globals_the_rom_s_routine_names_and_no_other` holds
  ev_multi's SOURCE to name `$c91a` itself, as the ROM's routine does; hoisted, the pin reds.
- **`savptr` named `certain` is a SPEED HINT**, held by the `AES_STEERED_FOR_NOTHING` sweep, with the one case it does
  not steer opted out by name (a poked key count that, inverted, is a queue too full to poll). Without the hint
  ev_multi's battery is 45 CPU-s cold.
- **Not swept by a generator**: `aes_event.py` and `bench/tier3.py` as wholes (hand mutants of what each agent
  changed); `pdpipe.S`, as before. **Not measured on a quiet machine**: the general guard's cost on `make bench`, the
  claim's back-off, the zygote's frozen check (0.1–0.2 ms a fork).

DEAD, proved from the ROM's bytes — not transcribed, or carried as bytes and never entered:
- disp's Line-F return `$fe4e00` (switchto ends in `rte` on every path); savestate's arm under the guard

THE LABELLED CASES (no ROM caller makes the machine):
- dsptch's `rts` under the guard (the lever's arm); mwait_act's "ready after all" arm and its event above the byte;
  gotopgm's staged basepage; disp_act's three argument-class machines (behind two processes, a process already last, a
  pointer queued with a top byte); disp's process neither ready nor waiting (PD_STAT `$0100`); idle's two (a woken
  process whose event has not come; a fork queued); ev_multi's argument class — six pointer-through-the-bus cases,
  fifteen overlaps, nine poked edges (the owner as a long, `$c836` and the pipe index signed, a key count of `$0100`
  and of `$8001`, `$c91a` halved, rlr's CDA against gl_cda both ways, an event bit no wait holds), `$97fe` staged set
  for the writer wakes (one poke, so the tail's clear is observable), and the EVB table past its end (the divergence
  above).

THE HOST MODEL'S LIMITS:
- a scheduled run that IDLES FOR EVER after deliveries is not kept; a process parked by a harness call
  (`aes_event.parked`) cannot be a FOREIGN process of a scheduled run — its continuation ends at the run's sentinel —
  and `aes_switch.scheduled` refuses such a run by name (a return "in another process"). The model is switched on per
  case; every other case refuses at dsptch.

KNOWN THIN MARGINS, both DERIVED checks now (a deeper frame of a later compiler reds by name, on a path no case runs as on the others):
- the button glue's private stack — 92 bytes, 78 used by our build (14 to spare; the ROM 70); the dispatcher's stack —
  640 bytes, 600 at the derived worst with a vertical blank and an MFP interrupt nested on top (40 to spare; the
  deepest measured run 300 / 312 + 244) — THE ROM'S OWN handlers' need and, since wave 18, OUR OWN ENTRIES', which
  are the ROM's instructions (under C bodies they needed 104 more, and the stack overran by 60). The 244 is the
  worst of every arm measured: timer C's tick that injects Alternate + an arrow's repeat is 144, every other 140.

DEFERRED, each measured or named:
- **THE KNOWN PRICING GAP (K5)** — the block under the Components table: the user's ruling.
- **The 16 MB image**: after the kit's two levers a fifth of the suite's CPU is still copying images (`make_image`:
  53,913 a run at the review); a lazily-zero mapping for the 14.6 MB of unmapped bus is counted, not prototyped, and
